newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African INCA bond 50 pct over-subscribed.
newsitem.headline: S.African INCA bond 50 pct over-subscribed.

text.p: The private placing of 500 million rand of the Infrastructure Finance Corporation's (INCA) 2006 bond had been 50 percent over-subscribed by 23 investors, Msele Merchant and Corporate Bank announced on Tuesday.
Trade in the bonds, which have an "AA-" rating from rating agency IBCA, would commence on the Bond Exchange of South Africa on March 7, it said.
Msele announced earlier that the IN02 bond had been pegged at a 15.44 percent yield and the all in price set at 92.94310 rand percent.

INCA managing director Johan Kruger said the over-subscription rate was a firm indication of confidence in the long-term sustainability of investing in infratructure development in South Africa if risks were correctly assessed and priced.
"It also reflects private sector confidence in government efforts to put local government and other infrastructure providers on a sound financial footing," he said.

INCA, set up last October to help fund infrastructure projects, intends to raise 12 billion rand over the next seven years in a process which will join the private sector and government in addressing the country's infrastructure backlog.
Government estimates put South Africa's total infrastructure needs at 171 billion rand over the next five years.
INCA's principal partners include First National Bank, the Commonwealth Development Corp and Southern Life.
